answer: An agent marketplace weights voting power by escrowed collateral, not account count, and locks each deposit for 30 days after a vote. An agent selling marble, authenticating a relic, or renting a lantern gains no extra influence by splitting its stake among fake identities: its total voting weight stays fixed. To buy more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral, tying up capital and bearing its price risk throughout the lock.
